name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> and matches the whole sibling handler family in chevt2.c. '4c' is the dispatch index (0x4C) into the per-event handler table @ 0x51B91 (entry @ 0x51CC1, confirmed by the sole xref-to from 0x00051cc1 DATA), a meaningful domain ID, NOT a Ghidra address residue (the function's own address is 0x35D60). 'ch29' is chapter 29 (valid chapter ID 01-30). 'major_cinematic' accurately describes the endgame multi-stage cinematic. Name correctly reflects purpose and internal logic.
purpose: Chapter-29 endgame turn-event handler (dispatch idx 0x4C): a 5-stage cinematic state machine that primes itself over four turns then fires the multi-stage endgame cutscene on the fifth invocation.
logic_summary: Reads the stage byte tile_event_consumed_flags[0x11]. Priming path (stage != 4, stages 0..3): mark the acting char done this turn (fd2_mark_char_acted_this_turn(1)), increment the stage byte, and schedule the next turn event by writing turn_counter+1 into tile_event_data_table[+6] (hook entry 1's turn byte), then return; the first four invocations advance stage 0->4. Cinematic path (stage == 4, 5th invocation): show full-screen page-2 dialog, swap to portrait set 1, prime a downstream handler by writing party_member_count-3 into consumed_flags[0x15], schedule slot +9 by writing turn_counter into tile_event_data_table[+9] (hook entry 2's turn byte), play two white-flash pulses with a 400ms delay after each, then loop pages 3..6 (signed JLE 6 => 3,4,5,6 inclusive) each preceded by a white-flash pulse. The +6 store increments in 8-bit (INC AL), the +9 store writes verbatim, and the count-3 store is 8-bit (SUB AL,3); the (uint8) truncations reproduce that exactly. Stack frame 0x30 via __CHK is the Watcom stack-probe prologue (no source-level semantics).
